candidate.answerReason: An odd sum of two primes must include 2, but the other summand would be 9999, which is composite.

methods.label: Use odd and even primes
methods.explanation:
Two odd numbers have an even sum, as do two even numbers. Since \(10001\) is odd, a prime pair summing to it must contain one even prime and one odd prime.

The only even prime is \(2\): every larger even number has \(2\) as a factor besides \(1\) and itself. Thus the other prime would have to be
\[
10001-2=9999.
\]
But the digits of \(9999\) sum to \(36\), so \(9999\) is divisible by \(3\). Since it is greater than \(3\), it is composite. The only possible pair therefore fails, leaving \(\boxed{0}\) ways, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary parity, the definition of a prime, and the digit-sum divisibility test for 3.

candidate.annotationRationale: Parity and prime-number structure reduce all possible representations to a single candidate pair. Factor meaning and the divisibility test for 3 support the rejection of that pair.

review.mathematicalCheck: An odd sum requires one even prime, necessarily 2. The other summand is 9999, which is greater than 3 and divisible by 3 because its digit sum is 36. Thus no prime pair exists.
